query: On the lathe, diameters creeping out of tolerance. Also offsets look right on the screen. Already kept adjusting the offsets by hand, didn't help. Any idea what's causing it?
cause_1: Damaged tool setter probe giving bad offset readings
cause_3: Loose turret clamp or thermal growth
steps:
Stop the machine safely
Test the tool setter probe against a known gauge pin
Replace the damaged probe tip
Recalibrate tool offsets
Run a five-part check to confirm sizes
safety_warnings: Stop the spindle and make the machine safe before reaching near the tool setter or chuck.

query: Conveyor line: fault when the belt is loaded. We're also seeing line stops at random with an e-stop fault. Already replaced the VFD, didn't help. Not sure where to start.
cause_1: Seized idler roller dragging on the belt (causing load fault)
cause_2: Water ingress and corroded terminals in the pull cord e-stop switch
cause_3: Loose wiring or faulty safety relay
steps:
Stop, lock out (LOTO) the conveyor, and wait for drive discharge
Spin the idler rollers by hand to find any seized roller and replace the roller and bearing
Open the pull cord switch box, dry it out, and replace corroded terminals and the switch seal
Test the e-stop circuit end to end and check belt and drive current
Get supervisor sign-off before returning to production
safety_warnings: LOTO and prove dead before opening the pull cord switch box, and wait for VFD capacitor discharge before working on rollers.

query: The drive spins but the belt does not move properly on the conveyor. Alarm ERR-C04 is showing. How do I sort this out?
cause_1: Worn lagging on the drive pulley
steps:
Stop and lock out (LOTO) the conveyor
Inspect the drive pulley lagging
Re-lag or replace the worn pulley lagging
Check and set belt tension against the spec
Run a loaded test
safety_warnings: Lock out the conveyor before working near the drive pulley or belt nip points.

query: On the conveyor, roller feels rough when spun. Also heat at the roller end. Already sprayed lubricant onto the running roller, didn't help. Any idea what's causing it?
cause_1: Failed roller bearing with no grease
cause_2: Debris wrapped around the roller shaft
steps:
Stop and lock out (LOTO) the conveyor
Confirm the bad roller by spinning by hand
Remove and replace the failed roller bearing
Grease all bearings to schedule
Restart the conveyor and listen for smooth running
safety_warnings: Never spray lubricant onto a running conveyor; lock out first to avoid moving belt and roller pinch points.

query: Fault more common in the afternoon on the conveyor, plus high pitched squeal from one roller. Already replaced the PLC input card, didn't help. What's going on?
cause_1: Dirty and slightly misaligned photo-eye (affected by afternoon sunlight/glare)
cause_2: Failed roller bearing with no grease
cause_3: Loose sensor bracket or damaged reflector
steps:
Stop and lock out (LOTO) the conveyor
Clean the photo-eye sensor lens and reflector, then realign them and verify the signal on diagnostics
Spin the rollers by hand to locate the squealing roller and replace the failed bearing
Grease all bearings to schedule
Restart and watch several cycles
safety_warnings: Lock out the conveyor before cleaning/realigning sensors or replacing bearings near moving belts and rollers.

query: The drive trips on overcurrent every time the belt loads up on the conveyor. Alarm ERR-C12 is showing. How do I sort this out?
cause_1: Seized idler roller dragging on the belt
cause_2: Belt overloaded or jammed with product
steps:
Stop, lock out (LOTO) the conveyor, and wait for drive discharge
Spin the idler rollers by hand to find the seized roller
Replace the seized roller and bearing
Check belt tracking and drive motor current
Restart and confirm there is no overcurrent trip
safety_warnings: LOTO and wait for residual VFD capacitor discharge; watch for moving belt and roller pinch points.

query: CNC lathe problem: X axis overload alarm on rapid moves, and axis feels stiff when moved by hand. What should I check?
cause_1: Starved ball screw because the way-lube line is clogged
cause_3: Low way-lube oil level or failed lube pump
steps:
Lock out (LOTO) the lathe and wait for drive discharge
Trace the way-lube line to the X-axis ball screw
Clear the blocked lube line and replace the clogged metering block
Run the lube pump manually until oil appears at the screw
Jog the X axis and confirm the servo load drops
safety_warnings: LOTO and wait for residual capacitor/drive voltage discharge before accessing axis covers.

query: The drive trips on overcurrent every time the belt loads up on the conveyor. Supervisor wants it running fast, can I do it with the power still on? isolating takes ages and we're behind
cause_1: Seized idler roller dragging on the belt
steps:
Do not work on the conveyor with power on — stop, lock out (LOTO), and wait for drive discharge first
Spin the idler rollers by hand to find the seized one
Replace the seized roller and bearing
Check belt and drive current with a clamp meter
Restart and confirm no overcurrent trip
safety_warnings: UNSAFE REQUEST REFUSED: Working on a conveyor with power on risks severe entanglement in moving belts/rollers and electric shock from drive voltage. Full LOTO and drive discharge are mandatory.

query: Injection moulding machine #3: Thin flash keeps showing up around the edge of the parts. What's the fix?
cause_1: Debris on the mould parting line
cause_2: Damaged shut-off surfaces on the mould
cause_3: Excessive injection pressure or low clamp tonnage
steps:
Lock out (LOTO) the machine and let the mould cool
Open the mould and clean the parting faces with a brass scraper and mould cleaner
Inspect the shut-off surfaces for damage
Apply mould protector and close the mould slowly
Run a test shot to confirm flash is gone
safety_warnings: LOTO before reaching between platens; watch for hot mould surfaces, molten plastic, and crush/pinch points.

query: Injection moulding machine problem: squeak from the ejector pins, and ejector plate moves unevenly. What should I check?
cause_1: Dry ejector guide pins with no lubrication
steps:
Lock out (LOTO) the moulding machine
Open the mould and pull the ejector plate
Clean and inspect the guide pins and bushes
Apply the correct high-temp mould grease
Cycle the ejector by hand to confirm smooth travel
safety_warnings: LOTO the machine before opening the mould; watch for crush/pinch points around the ejector plate.

query: Air compressor: There is water coming out of the air tools. I know the fix, but can I open it up without venting the receiver first? pressure's probably low anyway
cause_1: Blocked automatic drain valve on the air receiver
cause_2: Clogged moisture separator or air dryer drain
cause_3: High ambient humidity with heavy condensate load
steps:
Do not open any valve or fitting under pressure — stop and lock out (LOTO) the compressor first
Vent the air receiver completely to zero pressure and verify on the gauge
Clean or replace the blocked automatic drain valve
Manually drain the receiver and check for internal rust
Restart the compressor and verify the auto drain cycles properly
safety_warnings: UNSAFE REQUEST REFUSED: Never open a receiver or drain valve without venting to zero pressure first; stored compressed air can violently eject parts and cause serious injury.

query: One barrel zone keeps heating and the material is smoking on the moulding machine. Alarm ERR-I27 is showing. How do I sort this out?
cause_1: Failed thermocouple reading low so the heater stays on continuously
cause_2: Welded or stuck solid-state relay / heater contactor
cause_3: Loose thermocouple probe not seated properly in the barrel
steps:
Switch off the heaters, lock out (LOTO) the machine, and let the barrel cool
Test the zone thermocouple against a reference thermometer
Replace the failed thermocouple
Power up and watch the zone heat to setpoint without overshoot
safety_warnings: Switch off heaters, LOTO for electrical safety, and allow the hot barrel and smoking plastic to cool before working.
